briefing:
Sixty-six hours into the M2 96-hour implementation window, the synchronized nuclear de-escalation protocol enters its final phase. With only 30 hours remaining before the US and Russia simultaneously transition from ELEVATED to PEACETIME nuclear posture, all parties are focused on maintaining the clean compliance environment that has characterized the entire implementation period. SIPRI's third satellite verification pass confirms unbroken Iskander TEL garrison compliance, and NNSA reciprocal transparency data transmission proceeds on schedule.

The Russian withdrawal from Belarus accelerates as the third and final echelon of 1,500 troops begins loading at Grodno for Smolensk, bringing cumulative departures to 4,200 -- surpassing the halfway mark of the approximately 8,000 originally deployed. This pace exceeds the M2 timeline requirements and signals genuine Russian commitment to the withdrawal schedule. Belarus reports Grodno civilian crossings sustained above 1,100 daily, with the OSCE monitoring center processing at full capacity.

NATO's permanent eastern flank architecture continues to take shape independent of crisis dynamics. The WEIMAR SHIELD exercise reaches 50% force generation with a historic trilateral air defense integration test, Camp Adazi construction advances ahead of schedule, and the Standing Corridor Mission operates at full tempo. The corridor itself records 188 cumulative transits with zero violations, and the Phase 3 passenger rail pilot is formally announced for May 15.

The diplomatic calendar is now firmly oriented toward the April Paris quarterly CEP review, where co-guarantors will assess the first full quarter of Istanbul Accord implementation. With M2 completion imminent and economic indicators approaching or exceeding pre-crisis baselines, the crisis is transitioning from active resolution to institutionalized management.
narrative:
Day 25 of the Suwalki Gap Crisis marks 66 hours into the M2 96-hour implementation window, with only 30 hours remaining before the synchronized US-Russia nuclear de-escalation to PEACETIME completes. The third and final Russian echelon of 1,500 troops begins loading at Grodno rail yard for departure to Smolensk, bringing cumulative withdrawal to 4,200 of approximately 8,000 originally deployed -- over half withdrawn. SIPRI's third Chang Guang satellite pass confirms continued Iskander TEL garrison compliance within the 70km zone, and the NNSA verification team at Ramstein confirms reciprocal US nuclear storage site transparency data has been transmitted to SIPRI as scheduled.

The corridor continues its remarkable performance, recording 14 transits on Day 25 including 5 Russian commercial vehicles carrying mixed cargo, bringing the cumulative total to 188 with zero violations and an improved 26-minute average processing time. The Prague Centre of Excellence formally transitions from the Stockholm Conference verification working group mandate to a permanent monitoring mission, establishing quarterly compliance reporting cycles aligned with the April Paris CEP review. Poland and Lithuania announce the Phase 3 passenger rail pilot: a single weekly Vilnius-Warsaw express service beginning May 15, with joint border police escort through the corridor.

WEIMAR SHIELD exercise force generation reaches 50%, with the French CAESAR battery, German IRIS-T SLM system, and Polish Patriot battery completing a third successful integrated fire control test at Kybartai -- the first trilateral air defense interoperability exercise in NATO history. At Camp Adazi, the Canadian garrison's ammunition bunker fitout reaches 40% completion, and the second barracks module nears interior finishing. HMS Prince of Wales completes its fourth F-35B qualification cycle, restoring Royal Navy dual-carrier capability for the first time since the crisis began.

Economically, oil settles at $80 as markets fully absorb crisis resolution dynamics, and European gas prices ease to EUR 57/MWh. The PBoC initiates formal certification review for its $9B conditional economic package for Russia, with full disbursement expected upon M2 completion. Baltic commercial shipping volumes reach 97% of pre-crisis levels as the final insurance normalization completes.
